Cloud solution overview

Cloud Service Tenant General Requirements

1.       Cloud service tenant MUST ensure cybersecurity roles and RACI assignment is identified, developed, and approved for all stakeholders utilizing the Public Cloud Computing Service.

(SACS-212)(TPP3.3)

2.       Saudi Aramco information and data MUST be hosted and stored inside the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. (SACS-212) (TPP3.4)

3.       Prior to signing the contract, Cloud Service Tenant MUST ensure that the Cloud Service Provider is approved by Communications & Information technology Commission’s (CITC) and listed as a Class C Cloud Services Provider. (SACS-212)(TPP4.2)

4.       Data shared with a Cloud Service Provider, in any format, MUST be classified according to local classification requirements (TPP 5.2)

5.       Cloud Service Tenant MUST be registered in the centralized cloud asset inventory per “Asset Management Standard” (TPP5.1)

Cloud Service Tenant - Asset and Data Management

6.       Data leak prevention controls (e.g., Cloud Access Security Broker, SCP/DLP tools) MUST be implemented on the Public Cloud Computing Service to manage and protect sensitive data transferred or hosted at the CSP. (VPC traffic is excluded) (SACS-212)(TPP5.3)

Cloud Service Tenant - Identity and Access Management

7.       Centralized Identity and Access Management MUST be utilized to federate users’

identities to a corporate identity directory to authenticate and authorize users. (SACS-212) (TPP7.1)

8.       Multi-factor authentication for remote access and privileged cloud users MUST be implemented. (SACS-212) (TPP7.4)

9.       Cloud Service Tenant MUST utilize secure sessions management to include:

a)       session authenticity;

b)      session lockout;

c)       session timeout termination.

(SACS-212) (TPP7.6)

Cloud Service Tenant - Logging and Monitoring

10.   Cloud Service Tenant MUST activate and collect login event logs, and cybersecurity event logs on assets related to cloud services. Cloud Service Tenant may choose to utilize CSP, third party or the corporate centralized cybersecurity monitoring solution to monitor cybersecurity event logs. (SACS-212)

Cloud Service Tenant - Network and Encryption

11.   Sensitive Information MUST be encrypted at rest and during transmission. (SACS-330)

12.   Data exchange with external systems MUST be initiated from the internal network to the external resource (pull/push mechanism). NIST 800-53r5: AC-4 (7) SACS-340

Cloud Service Tenant - Penetration Testing

13.   The scope of penetration tests MUST cover Internet-facing services and its technical components including infrastructure, websites, web applications, mobile apps, email and remote access. (SACS-212)

14.   Penetration testing MUST be conducted periodically (SACS-212)

Cloud Service Tenant - Business Continuity – TIER 1 Applications

15.   Cloud Service Tenant MUST develop, implement, or contractually enforce business continuity and disaster recovery procedures for data entrusted to the Cloud Computing Service Provider. (SACS-212) (TPP11.2)

Cloud Service Tenant - Configuration Baseline

16.   Cloud Service Tenant MUST develop security configuration baseline based on the cloud service model (IaaS, PaaS and SaaS) and the baseline MUST be reviewed by an independent entity prior to moving the cloud service to production. (SACS-212)

Cloud Service Tenant - Vulnerability Management Controls – SACS320 (SSPM)

17.   Security configuration baseline must be developed, and approved (i.e., manager and security operations) prior to production use. Exceptions include Proof of concept (PoC) systems, in-house developed applications and standalone systems/applications that lack cybersecurity configurations.

18.   Security configuration and hardening baseline documentation for systems handling data must be reviewed as follows:

a) “Government Confidential” at least every six (6) months;

b) “Confidential”, “Company General Use”, and “Public” at least annually.

19.   Security configuration baselines must be monitored monthly via automated processes. In instances where automation is technically not feasible, a manual review must be conducted in-line with requirements in control VM 3.2.

Cloud Service Provider - API Controls

20.   Application Programming Interface (API) MUST be secured using the steps below.

a) input validation;

b) use tokens;

c) use encryption and signatures;

d) use quotas and throttling (where applicable);

(SACS-345)

21.   Access or refresh tokens MUST be issued by a centralized OAuth server. (SACS-345)

22.   APIs MUST be inventoried to include name, purpose, payload, usage and relationships between other APIs (if applicable). (SACS-345)

23.   API access tokens MUST be validated with every request. (SACS-345)

24.   A timeframe MUST be defined and enforced for access token expiry to reduce the risk of unauthorized access. (SACS-345)

Cloud Service Provider Controls

25.   Firewalls MUST be implemented at the network perimeter and only required services allowed. SACS-210

26.   Web Application Firewalls (WAF) MUST be utilized to inspect traffic (HTTP/S) from applications receiving traffic from the Internet. SACS-341

27.   All TLS web traffic communicated through the Web Application Firewall MUST be decrypted and inspected. SACS-341

28.   Cloud Service Provider MUST be protected from denial-of-service attacks (including Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS)). SACS-210

29.   TLS compression MUST be disabled. (SACS-330)

30.   Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) MUST be utilized for TLS connections. (SACS-330)

31.   Only server-initiated secure renegotiation MUST be utilized. (SACS-330)

32.   NOTE: This control can be removed if TLS1.3 is being used.

33.   At a minimum SHA-2 based certificates MUST be utilized. (SACS-330)

34.   Cybersecurity requirements for key management MUST be applied and reviewed periodically. (SACS-212) (TPP12.4).

Legal Analysis Summary:

For use by CCD only

Legal Analysis and Summary of Findings & Recommendations

 

Identified legal risks

1.       Data Hosting in Kingdom: Cloud Service Tenant shall ensure that no SAI data will be hosted out of Kingdom. Contracting attorney shall also ensure that the agreement restricts the hosting and storage of information to within the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia exclusively and no storage of SAI data outside of KSA.

2.       Data Privacy & Protection clause requirements within the agreement: The agreement with the vendor and any other party involved in the overall solution should contain sufficient obligations (extending to subcontractors) as it relates to data privacy and protection.

3.       Compliance with applicable Data Privacy & Protection Laws: Cloud Service Tenant must consider the local laws to ensure that the notice, collection and storage of personal data within the solution is in compliance with applicable laws.  In particular, KSA has issued the Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL).  The PDPL is effective from 23 March 2023.  The PDPL must be complied with, including:

           I.            Art.29. Art.29 requires the approval of the regulatory (the Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA) for any transfer or disclosure of Personal Data outside the Kingdom. This will be determined by the implementing regulations which are yet to be issued by SDAIA.

         II.            Privacy notice and consent. Personnel Dept. should ensure that an accurate privacy notice is in place for this solution as well as ensuring that consent from the applicable data subject has been obtained.

4.       Cybersecurity Terms and Conditions Section within the agreement: Contracting Dept. to ensure that agreement with the vendor contains the Cybersecurity Terms and Conditions “Schedule X”, including the Vendor/Contractor’s obligations clause to comply with the Saudi Aramco Third-Party Cybersecurity Standard (SACS-210).

Measures required to acceptably mitigate the identified legal risk

 

1.       Data Hosting in Kingdom: Cloud Service Tenant shall ensure that no SAI or Personal Data will be hosted out of Kingdom. Contracting attorney shall also ensure that the agreement restricts the hosting and storage of information to within the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia exclusively and no storage of SAI or Personal Data by vendor or its subcontractors outside of KSA.

2.       Data Privacy & Protection clause requirements within the agreement: The vendor’s agreement shall contain sufficient obligations as it relates to data privacy and protection.

3.       Compliance with applicable Data Privacy & Protection Laws: Law’s Corporate Compliance Department can support Saudi Aramco Cloud Service Tenant with the above requirements.

4.       Cybersecurity Terms and Conditions Section within the agreement: Contracting Dept. to ensure that agreement with the vendor contains the Cybersecurity Terms and Conditions “Schedule X”, including the Vendor/Contractor’s obligations clause to comply with the Saudi Aramco Third-Party Cybersecurity Standard (SACS-002).

 

 

 

 

 

 

1.      Introduction

1.1.            Cloud Cybersecurity Assessment (CCA)

Completing the CCA will provide Cybersecurity Governance Risk & Compliance Department (CGRCD) and Law’s Corporate Compliance Department (CCD) the information necessary to comprehensively evaluate, and consent to your Cloud Cybersecurity Assessment request as required by SACS-212 Third Party Proponent & Cloud Cybersecurity Standard. The evaluation will only be done once the cloud Service Tenant has obtained IT Demand Management approval on the required Cloud Computing solution.  A CCA should only be completed after the Cloud Service Tenant has finalized their selection of the specific Cloud Computing service to be used. However, the legal and security sections in the CCA can be used for guidance in selecting the appropriate Cloud Computing solution considering business and functional requirements. The Cloud Service Tenant must obtain concurrence, from the respective data owners, before hosting their data in the cloud.

The assessments provided by CGRCD and CCD are based solely on the accuracy and completeness of the information provided by the Cloud Service Tenant

The use of a Cloud Computing system, as described in this document, will require Cloud Service Tenant approval considering the analysis from CGRCD and CCD.

The CCA will ensure that:

·               Cybersecurity and legal risks are identified;

·               Risk mitigation measures can be identified and built into the project design;

·               Appropriate contract terms and conditions are in place to ensure compliance with applicable legal, regulatory and contractual requirements;

·               CGRCD and Law’s Corporate Compliance Department approval will be streamlined and consistent across the company; and

·               Formal sign-off is completed by the Cloud Service Tenant.

 

The role of CGRCD and CCD is to highlight any cybersecurity and legal risks in undertaking this cloud computing solution and EFFECTIVELY communicate the risks and legal issues involved. The decision to proceed with the cloud computing solution rests with Cloud Service Tenant. The purpose of the questions below are to enable the Cloud Service Tenant to make informed strategic choices within an acceptable legal risk profile to achieve the business objective

1.2.            Cybersecurity Terms and Definitions

Cybersecurity Term

Definition

Cloud Computing

Refers to any model that enables ubiquitous, convenient, on-demand network access to a shared pool of configurable computing resources (e.g. networks, servers, storage, applications and services) that can be rapidly provisioned.

 

Third-Parties

Refers to any party that is not a Saudi Aramco employee or contract worker nor an employee or contract worker of a Saudi Aramco subsidiary company.

Saudi Aramco information” “SAI

Refers to any information or data related to Saudi Aramco’s operations and activities and its employees, that was created, compiled, maintained, and/or received for Saudi Aramco use, regardless of the form or media in which the information is recorded or maintained. (GI 710.002).

 

Sensitive

Refers to information and data that is classified as “Confidential” or “Government Confidential”.  (GI 710.002).

 

Personal Data

Refers to any data, or collection of data, relating to an identified, or an identifiable, natural person, or data that can be reasonably linked to a specific computer or other device. An identifiable natural person is a person who can be identified, directly or indirectly, by reference to an identification number (e.g., an employee number, social security number or national identity card number) or factors specific to his or her physical, physiological, mental, economic, financial, cultural or social identity. (GI 1900.001).

 

Cloud Service Tenant (CST)

Is any natural or legal person (such as companies) who subscribes to the cloud computing services provided by the service provider.  As defined in (SACS-212)

 

Solution Integrator (SI)

Refers to a development entity with responsibility for developing a Cloud Computing service for Saudi Aramco.

Cloud Service Provider (CSP)

A cloud service provider (CSP) is an IT company that provides on-demand, scalable computing resources like computing power, data storage, or applications over the internet.

Data Owner

Refers to Any entity generating, acquiring, transmitting data.

 

1.3.            Completing the CCA

A legal Analysis Summary and Legal assessment (Section 5) are only required when a Cloud Computing solution contemplates:

·               hosting any Saudi Aramco Information (SAI) on a Cloud Computing system outside the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA);

·               hosting any SAI, that has not been classified as “Public” under GI 710.002 inside the KSA, on a Third-Party Cloud Computing system, where the Cloud Computing provider is not incorporated in KSA and is owned, registered, or operated by a company outside KSA.

 

Completing the CCA is not required for Proof of Concept (POC) but no company data is authorized to be uploaded to the POC Cloud unless the data has been sanitized or obfuscated in such a way that the data cannot be re-engineered back to Saudi Aramco data or have any resemblance to Saudi Aramco. In addition, the cloud service must not have any Saudi Aramco branding or pointers that this belongs to Saudi Aramco. Access must be restricted to a minimum number of users with a limited duration after which the cloud instance will be removed and deleted. The entity, using the cloud instance for the POC, must secure the cloud by following cloud service information security recommendations.

1.4.            Instructions for completing the CCA

All cloud solutions must first be approved by IT Demand Management before completing the CCA.

·               Step 1: Obtain IT Demand Management approval on the cloud solution before completing the CCA.

·               Step 2: Sections 2 & 3 of this CCA must be completed by the Cloud Service Tenant (CST) of the project.

·               Step 3: Section 4 & 6 must be completed by Cloud Service Provider (CSP).

·               Step 4: Legal Analysis Summary and Section 5 (Legal Assessment) must be completed by CCD.

·               Step 5: Security analysis to be completed by CGRCD.

·               Step 6: By signing the CCA, the Cloud Service Tenant (CST) confirms the accuracy of the information contained within the CCA.  By signing, the Cloud Service Tenant also confirms that it has understood and will comply with all of the requirements / restrictions / controls set out by CGRCD and CCD in Security Analysis Summary and Legal Analysis Summary of the CCA.  

·               Step 7: The Cloud Service Tenant (CST) must share the final version of the CCA with the assigned CGRCD analyst and CCD legal reviewer / attorney.

Reputation

Immaterial reputation impact.

Minor and/or temporary reputational impact with specific groups of internal stakeholders (employees, contractors, suppliers, customers, etc.)

Significant and/or lasting reputational impact with specific groups of internal stakeholders.

Widespread and enduring reputational impact with a wide range of internal stakeholders.

Localized negative media/public commentary.
Minor irritant to key relationships.
External stakeholders' (shareholders, regulators, analysts, etc.) concerns expressed privately.

Severe/sustained, localized negative media/public commentary.
Short term strain on key relationships.
External stakeholders' concerns expressed publicly.

Globally prominent, but temporary, negative media/public commentary.
Prolonged strain on key relationships and reduced confidence in management. Reduced social license to operate.

Globally prominent and sustained negative media/public commentary.
Severe/long-term damage to critical relationships and loss of confidence in management.
Revocation of social license to operate.

Strategy

Immaterial impact.

Failure of, or major delay to, achieving an objective regularly monitored at a Group level.

Failure of, or major delay to, achieving an objective regularly monitored at a Division level.

Failure of or major delay to achieving a Business Plan objective closely monitored at a Department level.

Failure of,or major delay to, achieving a key Business Plan  objective closely monitored at an Admin Area/GM level.

Failure of, or major delay to, achieving a key Business Plan objective closely monitored at a Business/Service Line level.

Failure, or major delay to, achieving a  strategic objective closely monitored at the Corporate level.

Failure of, or major delay to, achieving the overall Corporate strategic intent.

Immaterial interruption.

<1 day interruption not affecting customers.

1-7 days interruption not affecting customers.

>30 days interruption not affecting customers.

Health & Safety

Health & safety incident not requiring treatment.

Minor injuries requiring only first aid.

Lost time injuries. <10 recoverable injuries/illnesses  requiring hospitalization.

>10 recoverable  injuries/illnesses requiring hospitalization.

1-3 fatalities.
1-10 permanent disabilities or long term illnesses.

4-10 fatalities.

Environment

Immaterial environmental impact.

Single spill or release that is fully contained on site in bunds or tanks.

Single spill or release that is uncontianed but remains on site and is easily and rapidly rectified.

Environmental impact beyond the site (including groundwater or air emissions) with minor effect on the natural environment,  people or commerce.  Mobilization of facility resources is required in response.

Environmental impact beyond the site (including groundwater or air emissions) with moderate effect on the natural environment, people or commerce. Mobilization of extensive Company resources is required in response.

Widespread environmental impact, severely affecting the natural environment, people or commerce. Mobilization of multiple government agencies in response.

Widespread environmental impact, causing prolonged damage to the natural environment,  people or commerce. Mobilization of international incident response.

Comparable to worst environmental incidents in the industry (e.g., Deepwater Horizon, Kuwait oil fires).
